mainEntity.name: Which number matters more, systolic or diastolic?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both matter. Your category is set by whichever number falls in the higher band. After about age 50, systolic pressure becomes a stronger predictor of heart disease and stroke risk for most people.

mainEntity.name: Is one high reading a diagnosis of high blood pressure?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Diagnosis is based on the average of two or more readings taken on two or more occasions. A single high reading is worth rechecking, and repeated high readings are worth discussing with a clinician.

mainEntity.name: What is a normal blood pressure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Under the AHA categories, normal is a systolic below 120 and a diastolic below 80 mm Hg.

Under the AHA categories used here, yes: a systolic of 130 to 139 or a diastolic of 80 to 89 is stage 1 hypertension. One reading is not a diagnosis, so confirm it with repeated readings and a clinician.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between elevated blood pressure and stage 1 hypertension?

acceptedAnswer.text: Elevated means a systolic of 120 to 129 with a diastolic under 80. Stage 1 starts when the systolic reaches 130 or the diastolic reaches 80, whichever happens first.

mainEntity.name: What counts as a hypertensive crisis?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reading higher than 180 systolic and/or higher than 120 diastolic. Wait a minute and measure again. If it is still that high, contact your healthcare professional right away, and call 911 or your local emergency number if you have chest pain, shortness of breath, numbness, weakness, vision changes or difficulty speaking.

mainEntity.name: Do the blood pressure categories change with age?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The AHA categories apply to adults of any age. Average readings tend to rise with age, but that does not move the category cut-offs. Children and teens use age-based ranges instead.

mainEntity.name: How do I calculate pulse pressure and mean arterial pressure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pulse pressure is systolic minus diastolic, so 118/76 gives 42. Mean arterial pressure is about diastolic plus one third of the pulse pressure, so 118/76 gives 76 + 14 = 90 mm Hg.
